key.description: Human-readable name of the profile.

key.name: foreground-color
key.summary: Default color of text in the terminal
key.description: Default color of text in the terminal, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”).

key.name: background-color
key.summary: Default color of terminal background
key.description: Default color of terminal background, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”).

key.name: bold-color
key.summary: Default color of bold text in the terminal
key.description: Default color of bold text in the terminal, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”). This is ignored if bold-color-same-as-fg is true.

key.name: bold-color-same-as-fg
key.summary: Whether bold text should use the same color as normal text
key.description: If true, boldface text will be rendered using the same color as normal text.

key.name: cell-height-scale
key.summary: Scale factor for the cell height to increase line spacing. (Does not increase the font’s height.)

key.name: cell-width-scale
key.summary: Scale factor for the cell width to increase letter spacing. (Does not increase the font’s width.)

key.name: cursor-colors-set
key.summary: Whether to use custom cursor colors
key.description: If true, use the cursor colors from the profile.

key.name: cursor-background-color
key.summary: Cursor background color
key.description: Custom color of the background of the terminal’s cursor, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”). This is ignored if cursor-colors-set is false.

key.name: cursor-foreground-color
key.summary: Cursor foreground colour
key.description: Custom color for the foreground of the text character at the terminal’s cursor position, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”). This is ignored if cursor-colors-set is false.

key.name: highlight-colors-set
key.summary: Whether to use custom highlight colors
key.description: If true, use the highlight colors from the profile.

key.name: highlight-background-color
key.summary: Highlight background color
key.description: Custom color of the background of the terminal’s highlight, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”). This is ignored if highlight-colors-set is false.

key.name: highlight-foreground-color
key.summary: Highlight foreground colour
key.description: Custom color for the foreground of the text character at the terminal’s highlight position, as a color specification (can be HTML-style hex digits, or a color name such as “red”). This is ignored if highlight-colors-set is false.

key.name: enable-bidi
key.summary: Whether to perform bidirectional text rendering
key.description: If true, perform bidirectional text rendering (“BiDi”).

key.name: enable-shaping
key.summary: Whether to perform Arabic shaping
key.description: If true, shape Arabic text.

key.name: enable-sixel
key.summary: Whether to enable SIXEL images
key.description: If true, SIXEL sequences are parsed and images are rendered.

key.name: bold-is-bright
key.summary: Whether bold is also bright
key.description: If true, setting bold on the first 8 colors also switches to their bright variants.

key.name: audible-bell
key.summary: Whether to ring the terminal bell

key.name: word-char-exceptions
key.summary: List of punctuation characters that are treated as word characters
key.description: By default, when doing word-wise selection, most punctuation breaks up word boundaries. This list of exceptions will instead be treated as part of the word.

key.name: default-size-columns
key.summary: Default number of columns
key.description: Number of columns in newly created terminal windows. Has no effect if use_custom_default_size is not enabled.

key.name: default-size-rows
key.summary: Default number of rows
key.description: Number of rows in newly created terminal windows. Has no effect if use_custom_default_size is not enabled.

key.name: scrollbar-policy
key.summary: When to show the scrollbar

key.name: scrollback-lines
key.summary: Number of lines to keep in scrollback
key.description: Number of scrollback lines to keep around. You can scroll back in the terminal by this number of lines; lines that don’t fit in the scrollback are discarded. If scrollback_unlimited is true, this value is ignored.

key.name: scrollback-unlimited
key.summary: Whether an unlimited number of lines should be kept in scrollback
key.description: If true, scrollback lines will never be discarded. The scrollback history is stored on disk temporarily, so this may cause the system to run out of disk space if there is a lot of output to the terminal.

key.name: scroll-on-insert
key.summary: Whether to scroll to the bottom when text is inserted
key.description: If true, the terminal will scroll to the bottom when text is inserted by paste.

key.name: scroll-on-keystroke
key.summary: Whether to scroll to the bottom when a key is pressed
key.description: If true, pressing a key jumps the scrollbar to the bottom.

key.name: scroll-on-output
key.summary: Whether to scroll to the bottom when there’s new output
key.description: If true, whenever there’s new output the terminal will scroll to the bottom.

key.name: exit-action
key.summary: What to do with the terminal when the child command exits
key.description: Possible values are “close” to close the terminal, “restart” to restart the command, and “hold” to keep the terminal open with no command running inside.

key.name: login-shell
key.summary: Whether to launch the command in the terminal as a login shell
key.description: If true, the command inside the terminal will be launched as a login shell (argv[0] will have a hyphen in front of it).

key.name: preserve-working-directory
key.summary: Whether to preserve the working directory when opening a new terminal
key.description: Controls when opening a new terminal from a previous one carries over the working directory of the opening terminal to the new one.

key.name: use-custom-command
key.summary: Whether to run a custom command instead of the shell
key.description: If true, the value of the custom_command setting will be used in place of running a shell.

key.name: cursor-blink-mode
key.summary: Whether to blink the cursor
key.description: The possible values are “system” to use the global cursor blinking settings, or “on” or “off” to set the mode explicitly.

key.name: cursor-shape
key.summary: The cursor appearance

key.name: text-blink-mode
key.summary: Possible values are “always” or “never” allow blinking text, or only when the terminal is “focused” or “unfocused”.

key.name: custom-command
key.summary: Custom command to use instead of the shell
key.description: Run this command in place of the shell, if use_custom_command is true.

key.name: default-launch-entries
key.summary: Shells to spawn at startup, as (id, parent_id, name, directory, command, icon, color, color_target) tuples
key.description: Array of (id, parent_id, name, directory, command, icon, color, color_target) tuples describing the shells to open at axan startup when this profile is active. Each entry carries a stable UUID `id` (so the editor can reorder and reparent without breaking references) and a `parent_id` UUID identifying another entry in the same array (an empty `parent_id` means the entry is a root in the sidebar tree). `parent_id` must reference an entry earlier in the array — forward references only — so hierarchy can be applied incrementally as shells are spawned. `name` is an optional display-name template for the sidebar row; when non-empty it overrides the OSC-title fallback chain. Substituted at label-render time so live-derived names track directory changes. Supports: $pwd, $cwd, $dir, $~ (home-collapsed pwd), $user, $host, $hostname, $shell, $cmd, $title, $branch (git branch via .git/HEAD), $repo (basename of git toplevel), and ${file:path} which reads the first line (up to 128 bytes) of an arbitrary file — handy for piping external state into the label via a sidecar. Empty `name` keeps the existing fallback (OSC title, then directory basename, then "shell"). `directory` is the working directory; leading "~" expands to $HOME, absolute paths pass through unchanged, empty means "the directory axan was launched from". `command` is the program to run in the shell; empty means "the user's login shell". `icon` is an optional sidebar icon identifier: empty for the default status-glyph placeholder, `builtin:NAME` for a curated symbolic icon (terminal, ssh, database, package, container, git, editor, logs, build, test), an absolute filesystem path to a custom SVG/PNG, or a bare filename resolved against `~/.config/axan/icons/`. `color` is an optional per-node recolor token: empty for the theme foreground, one of the curated palette names (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple) which resolve to a theme-appropriate hex at render time (so the same value stays legible in light, dark, and future colorblind-safe themes — and stays portable in an exported TOML), or a literal `#RRGGBB` hex for advanced users who want a specific color (which does not adapt across themes). `color_target` selects which surfaces the recolor paints: `icon`, `text`, or `both`; empty is treated as `both`. The recolor paints symbolic glyph icons and/or the row label; custom image-file icons keep their own pixels. This setting is honored only when no shells were specified on the axan command line — any `--tab`, `--working-directory`, or positional command on the CLI takes absolute precedence. Empty array means "open one shell using the legacy default (your shell, in the launch directory)".

key.name: sidebar-state
key.summary: Sidebar collapse state
key.description: Whether the vertical-tabs sidebar is expanded (full row list with names, ~320px), collapsed (narrow column of initial-tab squares with a status glyph and a 2-char abbreviation), or minimized (thin strip with just the expand chevron, no cells). Cycled by the toolbar chevron or the cycle-sidebar accelerator. The value is shared across windows; a new window opens in whichever state was last set, so cycling once affects every sidebar.

key.name: startup-sidebar-state
key.summary: Sidebar state to apply when a new window opens
key.description: Controls what state the sidebar starts in for newly-opened windows. `last-used` (default) inherits the value of sidebar-state, so the sidebar opens in whatever state the last cycle left. The other choices pin every new window to that state regardless of any subsequent cycling.

key.name: collapsed-size
key.summary: Size step for the collapsed sidebar column
key.description: One of three discrete widths for the collapsed sidebar — small is the floor (just-fits-the-initials), medium leaves room for a glyph plus initials at comfortable spacing, large reserves enough width for a future icon slot. Concrete pixel widths are an implementation detail and may change between releases.

key.name: auto-assign-icon
key.summary: Automatically assign a sidebar icon to shells without an explicit one
key.description: When true, shells spawned without an explicit `icon` field in default-launch-entries get a built-in icon picked deterministically from the curated set, hashed off the shell's identity. When false (default), un-iconned shells render the status-glyph placeholder. An explicit icon string always wins over auto-assign; this only applies when no icon is set. Smart-match auto-assign by command or name keyword is filed as a follow-up (issue #400).

key.name: show-icons-in-expanded
key.summary: Show sidebar icons in the expanded row list
key.description: When true, the expanded sidebar prepends each row's icon (resolved the same way as in the collapsed view) before the row name — building muscle memory across both states. Default on: per-node icons and colors are a primary visual cue, and an icon you can't see in the main (expanded) view is a strange default. Turn it off for a strictly text-first tree.

key.name: recolor-icons
key.summary: Recolor custom SVG/PNG icons to match the theme foreground
key.description: When true (default), custom icons loaded from ~/.config/axan/icons/ are recolored to the theme foreground using their alpha channel as a mask — the same monochrome treatment the built-in symbolic icons get, so an imported set sits visually with the curated ones regardless of whatever fixed color the source SVG baked in. When false, custom icons render at their own colors. This only affects custom-file icons; built-in (`builtin:`) icons are always theme-recolored by GTK.

key.name: always-check-default-terminal
key.summary: Always check whether axan is the default terminal
